contradictions.description: Domain rules that detect logically / biologically contradictory records (e.g. blood pressure = 0, cholesterol = 0, p-tau > total tau, class 'no alcohol' with a positive alcohol measurement). Flagged values are reported raw and are excluded from later statistics.

rules.label: Age = 0
rules.description: Age 0 is not a plausible adult COVID-19 record; it is an unrecorded age.

rules.label: Impossible serum calcium
rules.description: Serum calcium outside 1.5-3.5 mmol/L. Values such as 20.25 are lab errors.

rules.label: Differential white-cell percentages do not sum to 100
rules.description: NE + LY + MO + EO + BA are percentages of white cells and must sum to about 100% (tolerance 2 points).

rules.label: Invalid coded value
rules.description: Sex and SARSCov must be 0 or 1.

rules.label: MCH inconsistent with haemoglobin / RBC
rules.description: MCH is derived as HGB / RBC * 10 (mismatch > 15%).

rules.label: MCHC inconsistent with haemoglobin / haematocrit
rules.description: MCHC is derived as HGB / HCT * 100. A mismatch > 15% indicates a transcription or unit error.

rules.label: MCV inconsistent with haematocrit / RBC
rules.description: MCV is derived as HCT / RBC * 10 (mismatch > 15%).

rules.label: Negative laboratory value
rules.description: Concentration / count measurements cannot be negative.

rules.label: Laboratory value = 0
rules.description: A zero in a concentration or blood count is used here as a missing code, not as a real measurement.

noise.description: Noise-to-signal analysis for tabular data: local k-NN residual noise divided by the robust signal spread, SNR(dB), Hampel spikes, repeated readings and out-of-range values. Each feature receives a verdict.

method.noise_to_signal: Robust sigma of the residual between each reading and the median of its 8 nearest neighbours in standardised feature space, divided by the robust sigma of the feature. 0 = perfectly predictable / smooth, 1 = as large as the signal itself. This is the tabular adaptation of the weather second-difference NSR (row order is meaningless in these tables).
method.snr_db: 10*log10(signal variance / noise variance); > 20 dB is very clean, < 5 dB is noisy.
method.spikes: Residual larger than 3.5 robust sigmas and 40% of the signal spread.
method.stuck_sensor: >= 10 identical consecutive readings on a continuous feature.
method.out_of_range: Values outside the biological / physical range; masked before stats.

model_phase.description: Model phase: target balance, sklearn Pipeline + ColumnTransformer, Random Forest on a stratified hold-out with 5-fold cross-validation, confusion matrix, and impurity / permutation / mutual-information feature importances.

preprocessing.pipeline: Median imputation + StandardScaler (numeric); most-frequent imputation + OneHotEncoder (categorical).

insights: Target 'SARSCov': {'0': 920, '1': 816} (balanced, ratio 1.13:1).
Hold-out: balanced accuracy 0.840, macro F1 0.842, accuracy 0.843 (majority baseline 0.530); ROC-AUC 0.898; 5-fold CV balanced accuracy 0.815 +/- 0.015.
Top permutation impact: 'LDH' (2.73 points of balanced accuracy).

model_lab.description: Modelling lab: three algorithms (KNN, Random Forest, SVM) compared with the same preprocessing (median imputation, one-hot encoding, auto-benchmarked scaler), tuned by explicit cross-validation loops (k, n_estimators, kernel/C), then evaluated on a stratified hold-out (accuracy, balanced accuracy, macro F1, ROC-AUC, overfitting gap) and stress-tested against noise and outliers (baseline / IQR-cleaned / feature noise / noise smoothed / injected outliers).

without_outliers.description: 129 row(s) removed with the IQR rule.

with_noise.label: With feature noise
with_noise.description: 18% Gaussian perturbation on every continuous feature.

noise_smoothed.label: Noise -> Gaussian smoothed
noise_smoothed.description: Noise injected then suppressed with gaussian_filter1d (sigma=1.2).

with_outliers.label: With injected outliers
with_outliers.description: 104 row(s) spiked at 3.5 sd on up to 3 features.

insights: Scaler benchmark chose StandardScaler; best model: Random Forest (Ensemble) (macro F1 0.824, balanced accuracy 0.823, ROC-AUC 0.8898).
Noise stress test: accuracy change -3.2 points with Gaussian noise (K-Nearest Neighbors); smoothing then changed it by -5.3 points. IQR cleaning: -0.7 points; injected outliers: -0.2 points.

Manual tuning winners: KNN {'n_neighbors': 7, 'metric': 'manhattan', 'weights': 'distance'} -> CV 0.775; Ensemble {'n_estimators': 50, 'max_depth': 10, 'class_weight': 'balanced'} -> CV 0.805; SVM {'kernel': 'rbf', 'C': 1.0, 'gamma': 'scale'} -> CV 0.800.

Gaussian smoothing is applied along the row order: on a table of unrelated patients it blurs distinct observations instead of removing sensor noise, which is why accuracy drops - keep it for time-indexed signals only.

Overfitting watch: K-Nearest Neighbors = High Overfitting Risk (Train 99.9% >> Test 79.0% (gap 20.9 points).); Random Forest = High Overfitting Risk (Train 97.5% >> Test 82.5% (gap 15.1 points).); Support Vector Machine = Moderate Overfitting (Train 88.5% > Test 81.3% (gap 7.1 points).).

recommendations.action: Correct the source values where possible; otherwise keep them masked as missing and document the domain rule that was violated.
Impute numeric features with the median and categorical features with the mode (already done inside the sklearn Pipeline); drop columns above 50% missing.

recommendations.finding: 'Age' contains 5 zeros where zero is not a valid measurement.
recommendations.action: Re-code these zeros as NaN before imputation; never let a placeholder enter scaling, correlation or model training.
Drop exact duplicates before cross-validation unless they are genuine repeated measurements; otherwise scores become optimistic.

recommendations.finding: 83.33% of tested features are flagged as noisy.
recommendations.action: Review the measurement protocol for the highest-NSR features; aggregate repeated readings or apply smoothing, and prefer robust scaling/tree models.

recommendations.finding: 18 value(s) outside the physical range were masked.
recommendations.action: Add the same range checks to the ingestion step and reject/log invalid readings instead of silently accepting them.
Inspect them with the domain expert; use robust models or winsorisation only when extremes are confirmed to be measurement errors.
Keep one of the pair, combine them, or use PCA / regularisation to avoid unstable importance and multicollinearity.

recommendations.finding: 'LDH' is the strongest impurity driver; permutation top is 'LDH'.
recommendations.action: Retain the top drivers but confirm they are available at prediction time; drop features whose permutation importance is near zero.
